data.title: Suspicious payment demand: "new bank details" from Stadtwerke
data.summary: A letter dated 7 September 2026 claims to be from Stadtwerke Musterstadt. It says the bank details have changed and demands €214.00 by 11 September 2026 to a new account, or the power will be cut off. It has strong signs of a scam.
data.explanation: This looks like a payment-redirection scam. Do not pay and do not call the special number in the letter. Contact Stadtwerke Musterstadt using the phone number or website from an earlier genuine bill or contract, and ask whether the letter is real. Real utilities rarely change bank details by an unsolicited letter and do not cut off power without notice. The payee is a foreign-style company (s.r.o.), not the utility. If you have already paid, contact your bank at once. You can also report it to the police or the consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale).

items.title: Demanded instalment payment (do not pay before verifying)
items.action: Do not pay. Verify the letter with Stadtwerke using contact details from a genuine earlier document.
items.consequence: The letter threatens to cut off the power without further notice, which is a pressure tactic.

warnings: The account holder is a different company (Global Energy Payments s.r.o.), not the Stadtwerke, which is a typical payment-redirection scam sign.
The letter threatens to cut off the power without notice and sets a deadline of only a few days, which is pressure typical of scams.
It tells you not to reply and to call only a mobile 'special number', which stops you checking it independently.
The sender email is on a generic domain (kundenservice-mail.example), and the letter has no greeting by name or invoice details.
Do not transfer money until you have checked with the utility using contact details you already trust.
